metadata.file_name: 89. Lee et al. (2025). Uncovering Behavioral Patterns in Creative Thinking: Utilizing and Interpreting PISA 2022 Process Data.pdf
metadata.title: Uncovering Behavioral Patterns in Creative Thinking: Utilizing and Interpreting PISA 2022 Process Data
metadata.abstract: Examining cognitive dynamics in the creative process is crucial for advancing creative theories and creativity education but has been historically understudied due to the technical challenges in collecting fine-grained data underlying cognitive processes. The PISA 2022 Creative Thinking assessment has the potential to address this limitation by offering rich, technology-based process data that capture cognitive and affective dynamics. To explore this potential, we outlined key topics and theoretical foundations in creativity research related to process data, followed by an illustrative example demonstrating how process data can illuminate creative thinking processes simply using descriptive statistics of released items. Furthermore, we delineated model-based approaches, including data mining techniques and extended item response theory models, to uncover various behavioral patterns in creative thinking through integrating process data and item responses together.

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This article is a review/synthesis of the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking (CT) process data and related model-based approaches. It does not report an original student-level predictive modeling analysis with an analytic sample drawn from PISA microdata, nor does it describe applying PISA complex survey weights or replicate-weight procedures. The only quantitative table (Table 1) reports descriptive ranges for released items and explicitly states values are sourced from the codebook for participating countries, not from a re-estimated weighted model. Therefore, survey-weight usage and replicate-weight usage are not applicable to the study’s presented methodology.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The paper is not an empirical predictive analysis of PISA 2022 CT achievement scores using plausible values (PVs). Instead, it reviews available PISA 2022 CT process metrics (e.g., response time, time to first action, actions, visits) and discusses descriptive and model-based approaches conceptually, including references to PVs in other contexts. Because no PV-based dependent variable is modeled in the article’s own analysis, PV handling and missing-data handling for an ML estimation pipeline are not applicable; additionally, the paper does not specify a missing-data strategy for an original dataset analysis.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic subsample is defined because the article does not conduct an original student-level empirical analysis. Table 1 reports descriptive statistics for two released PISA 2022 CT items and notes that the values represent all students in countries that participated in the CT assessment, sourced from the codebook.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2022 Creative Thinking process data (publicly released codebook statistics)
main_findings.target_variable: Cognitive and affective dynamics in creative thinking (PISA 2022 CT process data review)
top_predictors: See outcome_summary (descriptive associations not coded as predictors)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Descriptive statistics for 3 released PISA 2022 CT items (Table 1 / Table A2): Robot Story item 1 (Generating diverse ideas, Written expression): M total time = 337s (SD = 166, P5 = 52, P95 = 760, Med = 321), M time to first action = 23s (SD = 16), M actions = 428 (SD = 307, P95 = 1172, Max = 6091), M visits = 1 (Max = 5); Save the River item 1 (Generating diverse ideas, Scientific problem-solving): M total time = 209s (SD = 93), M actions = 174 (SD = 122, Max = 1893); Save the River item 2 (Evaluating and improving ideas): M total time = 151s (SD = 71), M actions = 120 (SD = 95, Max = 3305). PISA disengagement threshold: responses < 15s treated as missing; rapid responding < 30s. No ML performance metrics (no predictive models estimated).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: This review maps 5 PISA 2022 CT process metrics onto creativity research constructs (serial order effect, cognitive styles, engagement/disengagement). Descriptive patterns from released items show Robot Story elicits more actions (M = 428) and more revisits (Max = 5) than Save the River items (M actions = 174 and 120 respectively, Max visits = 1), suggesting domain context and ideation facet shape process behavior. The paper recommends theory-grounded analysis approaches (clustering, mixture IRT) for future research but does not provide policy-actionable predictions.

data.outcome_summary: This is a conceptual review and methods paper that describes the 5 PISA 2022 Creative Thinking process data metrics (total time on item, time to first action, number of actions, number of visits, number of short visits) and their theoretical grounding in creativity research. An illustrative example uses publicly available descriptive statistics for 3 released items from 2 units (Robot Story item 1; Save the River items 1 and 2). The paper further outlines model-based approaches (data mining, mixture IRT) suitable for analyzing process data in creativity research, but does not conduct any primary analysis. No ML models are trained; no student-level outcomes are predicted.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The manuscript is a review/survey paper that outlines topics, theoretical foundations, and model-based approaches for analyzing PISA 2022 CT process data. It does not report an original empirical ML pipeline with a defined analytic sample, country-level sample sizes, or trained/evaluated machine learning models; consequently, total_students, countries/n_students, ML techniques, and structured predictive findings are not extractable from the provided text.
